definition: Azure Policy evaluates Azure resources against governance rules and can apply effects such as audit or denial.
example: An administrator audits whether deployments use approved geographic regions.

definition: Azure Security refers to protecting Azure workloads and data through identity, network, configuration, and monitoring controls.
example: A cloud team restricts storage access to approved identities and monitors for unauthorized changes.
sense_note: This is a broad practice, not necessarily a single Microsoft product.

definition: Babylon.js is a JavaScript and TypeScript engine for rendering and interacting with 3D scenes on the web.
example: A developer adds an interactive product model to a browser-based showroom.

definition: Back-end development implements the services, storage, and business logic that support client applications.
example: A developer builds an order service that checks inventory before saving a purchase.

definition: Backbone.js is a JavaScript library that structures web applications using models, collections, views, and routing.
example: A maintainer updates how a Backbone view responds to changes in its underlying data.

definition: BACnet is a communication protocol for exchanging data among building automation and control systems.
example: A facilities dashboard reads room temperatures from compatible heating and ventilation controllers.

definition: Bacon.js is a JavaScript library for modeling changing values and asynchronous events with functional reactive streams.
example: A web interface combines a filter selection stream with a search text stream.

definition: Bacterial culture is the growth of bacteria in a controlled laboratory setting for observation, identification, or study.
example: A microbiologist reviews a culture report to distinguish growth from a negative result.

definition: The balafon is a wooden-key percussion instrument, usually with resonators beneath its keys, used in West African musical traditions.
example: An ensemble player performs a repeating melodic pattern on a balafon.

definition: Balloon modelling shapes inflated balloons into recognizable figures or decorative structures.
example: A performer twists balloons into a simple animal for an event.

definition: Banner advertising places visual promotional units within websites, apps, or other digital displays.
example: A campaign team checks whether a display banner is legible at its intended dimensions.

definition: Banyan VINES was a network operating system that provided directory, file, and other network services.
example: An IT historian examines how a legacy office network organized users and shared printers.

definition: The Baseline Personnel Security Standard is a UK government framework for basic employment screening of individuals with access to government assets.
example: A recruiter documents completion of the required baseline checks before a new staff member begins work.
sense_note: This is a baseline screening framework, not a national security clearance.

definition: BaseX is an XML database and XQuery processor for storing and querying structured documents.
example: A publishing team retrieves sections of manuals by querying their XML markup.

definition: Batman.js was a JavaScript framework for building client-side web applications around models, bindings, and views.
example: A maintainer troubleshoots an obsolete application whose page automatically updates when its data changes.

definition: Battle management is the coordination of situational information, decisions, and resources during military operations.
example: A historian studies how a command structure divided responsibility for tracking events and reporting decisions.

definition: Bed mobility is the ability to reposition oneself in bed or the clinical support needed to perform those movements.
example: A therapist observes how independently a patient can roll and move into a seated position.

definition: Behavior change communication uses audience research and designed messages to support adoption or maintenance of a specific behavior.
example: A community program tests which reminders make attendance at scheduled health appointments easier.

definition: Benefits realisation management defines intended gains from an initiative and tracks whether they occur after implementation.
example: A project sponsor assigns responsibility for checking processing time several months after a new workflow launches.

definition: Bereavement care provides practical, emotional, and, when appropriate, clinical support to people grieving a death.
example: A care team offers a family information about local grief support and follows up after the funeral.

definition: The Berkeley Data Analytics Stack was a research software ecosystem integrating tools for distributed processing and analysis of large datasets.
example: A researcher studies how its projects combined cluster computing with analytics workloads.

definition: Bidirectional-streams Over Synchronous HTTP is a transport specification that emulates a two-way stream using sequences of HTTP requests and responses.
example: A messaging client exchanges streaming messages over ordinary HTTP infrastructure.

definition: BigFix is an endpoint-management platform for tracking device inventory, distributing software, and applying patches or configuration policies.
example: An administrator checks which managed devices still need an approved update.

definition: Binary Ninja is a reverse-engineering platform for examining compiled software through disassembly and intermediate representations.
example: A defender reviews an unknown executable’s high-level behavior as part of incident triage.

definition: BIND is a software implementation of the Domain Name System used to serve authoritative DNS answers or resolve names.
example: An administrator validates a zone change before publishing it on a nameserver.

definition: Bioconductor is a collection of R packages and data resources for analyzing biological and genomic datasets.
example: A researcher generates exploratory plots from a published gene-expression dataset.

definition: Biopython is a collection of Python libraries for working with biological data formats and computational biology tasks.
example: An analyst reads annotation records from a public sequence database into a table.

definition: Bitly is a link-management service that creates shortened URLs and measures interactions with them.
example: An event team compares clicks on links printed on two different flyers.

definition: BlackLine provides software for managing reconciliations, close tasks, and related accounting controls.
example: An accounting team records a balance reconciliation and routes it for sign-off.

definition: Blast radius analysis estimates which systems, users, or operations could be affected by a proposed change or failure.
example: A team maps which applications depend on a database before scheduling its maintenance.

definition: Blended learning purposefully combines in-person instruction with online or computer-mediated learning activities.
example: Learners review demonstrations online and use class time to practice with instructor feedback.

definition: Blender Game Engine was Blender’s integrated runtime and authoring environment for interactive 3D experiences.
example: An archivist opens a legacy project in a compatible Blender version to inspect its logic bricks.
sense_note: The historical Blender component is distinct from later forks and unrelated engines.

definition: Boa Constructor was a Python development environment and GUI builder for applications using wxPython.
example: A maintainer opens a legacy desktop dialog and edits the layout visually.

definition: A board support package contains the code and configuration needed to run an operating system on a particular hardware board.
example: An embedded developer uses the package to initialize a board’s supported peripherals at boot.

definition: Body contouring refers to surgical or nonsurgical procedures intended to change the shape of a region of the body.
example: A clinician discusses which contouring options, risks, and recovery expectations are relevant to a patient’s goals.

definition: BODYATTACK is a branded group fitness class built around aerobics, athletic movement, and conditioning exercises.
example: An instructor demonstrates a low-impact alternative during a group session.

definition: BODYPUMP is a branded group fitness class using repeated resistance exercises performed with barbells or weights.
example: A participant selects an appropriate load for the class’s squat track.

definition: Bonjour is Apple’s zero-configuration networking implementation for local network service discovery and name resolution.
example: A laptop discovers a compatible network printer without requiring its address to be entered manually.

definition: Boolean search combines search terms using logical operators to include, require, or exclude conditions.
example: A recruiter searches for analyst profiles that mention either Python or R while requiring a specified location.

definition: The Box API provides programming access to Box content, users, permissions, and related services.
example: An authorized integration uploads a report to a designated team folder.
